panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (a, b, c, d). a: Clinical photograph of the right great toenail in a patient with onychomatricoma, showing the captioned thickened and overcurved affected nail plate. b: Clinical photograph after partial removal of nail polish, showing captioned dystrophy and pitting of the affected right great toenail in onychomatricoma. c: Intraoperative clinical view after nail plate removal shows the captioned matrix tumor with finger-like projections, characteristic of onychomatricoma. d: Gross image of the undersurface of the removed nail plate showing numerous spicules, a characteristic onychomatricoma finding described in the caption.
panels.attribution_text: Romero et al. Onychomatricoma Presenting as a Dystrophic Right Great Toenail: Case Report and Review.. Cureus 2020. doi:10.7759/cureus.7946. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Onychomatricoma of the right great toenail of a 43-year-old woman There is nail polish on both great toenails; however, the affected right great toenail (black arrow) is thickened and shows overcurvature (a). After partial removal of the nail polish, the right great toenail shows dystrophy and pitting (black arrows) (b). After the nail plate has been removed, the right great toe reveals a tumor (black arrow) with finger-like projections (c). The undersurface of the removed nail plate has numerous spicules (bent black arrows) (d).
in_text_mentions: Cutaneous examination revealed a nontender right great toe. There was diffuse nail dystrophy with proximal nail fold thickening and scale. All of her fingernails and other toenails were normal in appearance (Figure 1).

The patient underwent an excisional biopsy three months later including both nail bed and the nail matrix down to bone. The nail plate was avulsed. A tumor with finger-like projections arising from the nail matrix was revealed (Figure 1). In addition, the nail plate had spicules.

in_text_mentions: Next, we searched for pathologic conditions arising from the specialized nail tissue we defined. Onychomatricoma is a tumor arising within or in the vicinity of the nail matrix (Fig. 5a–c). We hypothesized that onychomatricoma is arising from onychofibroblasts22 and evaluated CD10 expression in onychomatricoma (Fig. 5f, h). We found that CD10 was strongly expressed in the mesenchymal part of the tumor.
